chapter: The Grid (levels 71-80, the neon wireframe world of mathematical solids) - regenerated on the desert's ember model (the owner, 2026-10-11, #824): a lead line the ear can follow, its identity in the mid range, the drive carried by arrangement rather than by noise and sub bass; the family's electronic dance root kept
purpose: Master of Game/Music/pulse-progressive.ogg: written from this file by Tools/MusicBake --tracks --masters <this folder>, brought to the themes' loudness, peaks held under full scale, Ogg Vorbis. The master stays outside the repository (C:/Users/panrd/AI/output/masters-824-chosen on the desktop, with its .raw.wav; every candidate in masters-824); this sidecar is committed beside the .ogg.
generator: ACE-Step 1.5 (acestep.cpp v0.0.5), local, AMD RX 6900 XT via Vulkan -- batch-pulse.ps1 -> generate-music.ps1 -Loop -NoCotCaption
format: 48000 Hz, 32-bit float PCM, stereo -- 48 kHz is the model's fixed native rate

request.caption: Melodic progressive house instrumental for a neon wireframe world of glowing geometric shapes: a long, memorable synth lead melody you can hum carried in the mid range, evolving plucked synth arpeggios beneath it, a warm rolling bass line in the mid range, warm wide chord pads, a punchy four-on-the-floor kick with a dark snare clap and toms and a dark ride cymbal playing throughout, the melody passing between a warm pluck and a soft analog lead over the unbroken groove, building and glowing into a big warm peak with wide synth chords, hopeful and spacious, warm mid-forward mix, modern polished production, wide stereo mix with instruments panned left and right, stereo delays, spacious reverb, no vocals
request.lm_negative_prompt: vocals, singing, choir, humming, sampled vocal chops, vocoder, talk box, audience applause, crowd noise, live recording, comedy, cartoon, silly, childish, cute, sugary, toy piano, music box, ambient drone, free tempo, rubato, long quiet intro, long silent passages, boomy sub bass, 808 sub bass, deep sub bass, rumble, distorted bass, growling bass, wobble bass, white noise, noise sweeps, risers, hiss, glitch, siren synths, industrial noise, bright supersaw, fizzy synths, sizzling high synth leads, airy shimmer, sparkling high chimes, bright crash cymbals, splashy cymbals, cymbal wash, open hi-hats, sizzling hi-hats, bright hand claps, tambourine, shakers, snare rolls, long drum-only sections, drum solo, harsh dissonance, quiet breakdown, near silence, long soft passages, fade out, fade in, long soft intro, droning, one-note bass

chosen.why: inside ember on every column: 29.5 % in 200 Hz-2 kHz (old 8.4 %), 20.3 % in 300 Hz-4 kHz, 0.4 % above 6 kHz, tonal mid 93 %, 4.03 held-note changes/s, a 45 s loop in time (context 0.55, crossfade r 0.65 against 0.43, spectrum cos 0.71), no hole, wrap step -0.6 dB (p16), the widest stereo of the family (L/R 0.48). It has no drums for a layer to take (Demucs found them 42 dB under the mix), so the old layer is gone. c2 is 3.4 % above 6 kHz
chosen.how: every candidate measured with Tools/Generation/measure-music.py --reference ember in one run (band shares, tonal mid, mid flatness, held-note changes, tempo wander, wrap step) beside the loop cut's own check, the hole share (the loop more than 10 dB under its loud level), the breakdown dip and the stereo correlation; a seam below its own rhythm, a hole over 15 %, a 2 s dropout more than 20 dB down, a wrap step of 10 dB or more or at or above p97 of the loop's own steps, a seam spectrum cosine under 0.3 or a loop under 30 s ruled a candidate out; the table is on #824
